editorial:
Imagine trying to film your own father while he is slowly dying. That is exactly what KG Forsberg does in this quirky story. He is a documentary filmmaker who decides to turn his family tragedy into a project, which creates a really weird and funny tension between him and his dad. You get to see a relationship that is honestly a bit messy, but it feels real. It is not your typical sad movie about death because it mixes in a lot of dry humor that makes the heavy stuff easier to handle.

The acting is great because it feels like you are just eavesdropping on a real family. The pacing is slow and steady, which lets you really feel the emotions, though some might find it a bit too quiet. If you like stories that find light in dark places, you will love this. Since it is an older TV movie, you might want to track down a high-quality digital version. You can try renting it on Apple TV or adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality. It is a perfect pick for a rainy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up as KG finally stops treating his father like a subject in a movie and starts treating him like a dad again. After all the filming and tension, the father eventually passes away. KG is left with his footage, but he realizes that the real value was in the time they spent talking. He finds peace with his loss, and the film ends on a quiet, honest note about saying goodbye.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic family dramas and dry humor.
